subclasses.name: The Archfey
subclasses.summary: Your patron is a powerful lord or lady of the Feywild whose goals are whimsical and hard to read. Its gifts center on enchantment, charm, fear and slipping away in mist.

features.name: Fey Presence
features.summary: Action: every creature within a 10-foot cube centred on you must make a Wisdom save against your warlock spell save DC. Each one that fails is charmed or scared (your pick) until your next turn ends. Recharges on a short or long rest.

features.name: Misty Escape
features.summary: Reaction when you take damage: vanish and reappear as an invisible figure up to 60 ft away in any open spot you can see. The invisibility lasts until your next turn begins, or until you make an attack or cast a spell. Recharges on a short or long rest.

features.name: Beguiling Defenses
features.summary: You cannot be charmed. When someone tries to charm you, you can use your reaction to force a Wisdom save against your spell save DC; on a failed save it becomes charmed by you for a minute, ending early if it takes damage.

features.name: Dark Delirium
features.summary: Action: target a creature you see within 60 feet; Wisdom save vs your spell save DC. On a failure it is charmed or frightened (your choice) for 1 minute, requiring your concentration, ending early if it takes damage. It believes it is in an illusory misty realm you design and perceives only itself, you and the illusion. Recharges on a short or long rest.

subclasses.name: The Fiend
subclasses.summary: You have bargained with a being from the lower planes whose aims are evil. It rewards you with fire magic, durability and the ability to hurl foes into hell.

features.name: Dark One's Blessing
features.summary: Dropping a hostile creature to 0 HP grants you temp HP equal to your Charisma modifier plus warlock level (at least 1).

features.name: Dark One's Own Luck
features.summary: When you make an ability check or saving throw, add 1d10 to the roll, even after seeing it but before the outcome. Recharges on a short or long rest.

features.name: Fiendish Resilience
features.summary: After a short or long rest, choose one damage type to gain resistance to, until you choose another. Damage from magical or silver weapons ignores this resistance.

features.name: Hurl Through Hell
features.summary: When you hit a creature with an attack, you can send it through the lower planes; it vanishes and returns at the end of your next turn to its space or nearest open one. A non-fiend takes 10d10 psychic damage. Recharges on a long rest.

subclasses.notes2024: In the 2024 PHB the Fiend patron is renamed Fiend Patron; Dark One's Blessing and Hurl Through Hell are reworked (Hurl Through Hell costs a Pact Magic slot rather than a rest use).

subclasses.name: The Great Old One
subclasses.summary: Your patron is an alien entity from beyond reality, indifferent or unaware of you, whose vast knowledge grants psychic and mind-bending powers.

features.name: Awakened Mind
features.summary: You can speak telepathically to any creature you see within 30 feet, with no shared language needed, though it must understand at least one language.

features.name: Entropic Ward
features.summary: Reaction when a creature attacks you: impose disadvantage on that roll. If it misses, your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn has advantage. Recharges on a short or long rest.

features.name: Thought Shield
features.summary: Your thoughts cannot be read by telepathy or other means unless you allow it. You resist psychic damage, and any creature that deals psychic damage to you takes the same amount.

features.name: Create Thrall
features.summary: Action: touch an incapacitated humanoid to charm it until remove curse is cast on it, the charmed condition is removed, or you use this feature again. You can communicate telepathically with it while on the same plane.

subclasses.notes2024: In the 2024 PHB this is the Great Old One Patron with reworked features (e.g. Psychic Spells, Clairvoyant Combatant).

subclasses.name: The Celestial
subclasses.summary: Your patron is a being of the Upper Planes, and your magic leans toward healing and radiant fire. You gain a pool of healing dice, extra light-themed cantrips, and a spell list full of restorative and fiery spells.

features.name: Expanded Spell List
features.summary: The Celestial adds extra spells to the warlock spell list for you, from 1st through 5th spell level (see granted spells).

features.name: Bonus Cantrips
features.summary: You learn the light and sacred flame cantrips. They do not count against your number of cantrips known.

features.name: Healing Light
features.summary: You have a pool of d6s equal to 1 + your warlock level. As a bonus action, pick a creature you can see within 60 feet and spend up to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) dice from the pool; roll them and the creature regains that many hit points. You regain all spent dice when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Radiant Soul
features.summary: You gain resistance to radiant damage. When you cast a spell that deals radiant or fire damage, you add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll of that spell against one of its targets.

features.name: Celestial Resilience
features.summary: Whenever you finish a short or long rest, you gain temporary hit points equal to your warlock level + your Charisma modifier. In addition, choose up to five creatures you can see at the end of that rest; each gains temporary hit points equal to half your warlock level + your Charisma modifier.

features.name: Searing Vengeance
features.summary: When you would make a death saving throw at the start of your turn, you can instead spring back up: you regain hit points equal to half your hit point maximum and may stand without spending movement. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet then takes radiant damage equal to 2d8 + your Charisma modifier and is blinded until the end of the current turn. Once used, you must finish a long rest before using it again.

subclasses.notes2024: The 2024 Player's Handbook reprints this patron as the Celestial Patron with revised features (Healing Light, Radiant Soul, Celestial Resilience, Searing Vengeance).

subclasses.name: The Hexblade
subclasses.summary: A warlock who pacts with a mysterious force from the Shadowfell, the Hexblade fights as a martial caster in medium armor, using Charisma for weapon attacks. They brand foes with a curse that boosts damage and crit chances, and later raise spectral minions from slain humanoids.

features.name: Hexblade's Curse
features.summary: As a bonus action, curse a creature you can see within 30 feet for 1 minute. The curse ends early if the target dies, you die, or you are incapacitated. While it lasts: you add your proficiency bonus to damage rolls against the cursed target; your attack rolls against it score a critical hit on a 19 or 20; and if it dies, you regain hit points equal to your warlock level + your Charisma modifier (minimum 1). Once used, it must be recharged with a short or long rest.

features.name: Hex Warrior
features.summary: You gain proficiency with medium armor, shields and martial weapons. At the end of a long rest you may touch one weapon you are proficient with that lacks the two-handed property; until your next long rest, you use your Charisma modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls. If you later take Pact of the Blade, this extends to every pact weapon you create, whatever its type.

features.name: Accursed Specter
features.summary: When you slay a humanoid, you can have its spirit rise as a specter under your control. It appears in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of the corpse, uses the standard Specter stat block, gains temporary hit points equal to half your warlock level, and adds your Charisma modifier (minimum +0) to its attack rolls. It acts on its own initiative count, obeys your commands, and vanishes at the end of your next long rest. Once used, you must finish a long rest before using it again.

features.name: Armor of Hexes
features.summary: If the target of your Hexblade's Curse hits you with an attack roll, roll a d6. On a 4 or higher, the attack instead misses you, regardless of its roll.

features.name: Master of Hexes
features.summary: When a creature cursed by your Hexblade's Curse dies, you can immediately apply the curse to a different creature you can see within 30 feet of the dead one, without expending a use of the feature. You cannot do this if you are incapacitated, and the new curse works normally for the remainder of its duration.

subclasses.notes2024: Not reprinted in the 2024 Player's Handbook.
